Subject: sudden p95 increase on sierra-v3 — asking for rollback / SLA relief

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency for the sierra-v3 model used by our account yesterday evening. The spike is concentrated on longer prompts (>700 tokens) and is impacting critical real-time flows for our payments product — timeouts are starting to occur in the checkout path.

Attached are the trace captures and a CSV with hourly p95 for the last 48h. This is customer-impacting, and we need a mitigation path: either a rollback to the previous variant (sierra-v2-stable) or a formal SLA carveout while you remediate.

Can you confirm the estimated time to switch back to v2 and whether Redwood can provide a temporary SLA exception (we will need written confirmation for our internal incident report)? We also need an estimate of any billing impact / credits while the exception is active.

Thanks — Kara

Attachments: sierra-p95-metrics-20260615.csv, corefinance-evidence.zip

Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on sierra-v3 — asking for rollback / SLA relief

We ran a quick assessment against the telemetry Kara attached and our internal traces. Preliminary findings: a regression in the attention kernel selection for long-context requests on the sierra-v3 quantized path — it increases token-level latency for sequences >700 tokens.

Mitigation options (tradeoffs in parentheses):
- Emergency prefix: pin CoreFinance to sierra-v2-stable (~30–45m). Pros: immediate p95 reduction. Cons: slight quality delta for a subset of prompts.
- Roll-forward patch to sierra-v3 (targeted kernel recompile) — ETA 6–12 hours, lower risk to quality but longer exposure window.
- Traffic shaping (rate-limit long requests) — will degrade UX for heavy flows.

I recommend the pin to v2 now, then a controlled rollout of a v3 patch overnight with validation on a canary. If approved, ops will: 1) mirror traffic to v2 for 15m for validation, 2) switch 100% and monitor p95 for 60m, 3) keep rollback plan open.

Dashboard (live): https://dash.redwood.internal/metrics/corefinance/sierra-v3/p95

Priyom Das
